card: Updates doc/i2p.md to clarify that connections created under -privatebroadcast use dedicated one-time transient destinations rather than the persistent I2P address. This resolves an omission in the documentation that could mislead node operators about persistent address reuse across connection types. The change is documentation-only with no code modifications.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete patch showing exact phrasing additions in doc/i2p.md; the scope and intent are unchanged.
evidence: PR description: 'It is not entirely accurate that persistent I2P addresses are used for making outbound connections and accepting incoming ones, as the -privatebroadcast option forces the use of a new transient destination for each transaction it relays.'
problem: doc/i2p.md stated that persistent I2P addresses are used for making outbound and accepting inbound connections without noting the exception introduced by transaction private broadcasts, giving node operators an incomplete picture of their I2P network footprint.

risk.why: Modifies documentation only, carrying no runtime or consensus risk.

summary: Clarifies in the I2P documentation that the persistent I2P address is not used for all outbound connections. It documents that when -privatebroadcast is enabled, Bitcoin Core opens connections using a one-time transient address for each transaction relay regardless of -i2pacceptincoming settings.
